# shiv

An AI assistant that runs in your terminal, on the device.

Talk to a model, let it run commands, keep the conversation across sessions. Sign in to OpenRouter through the browser, or paste your own key for any other provider. Since **2.0** it can also build tweaks, end to end, without leaving the phone.

## What it does

**Reads and edits files, runs shell commands** — shell commands and file writes always ask first. What counts as "ask every time" is set in `/permissions`.

**Sessions** are saved every turn. Resume the last one, pick an earlier one, or rewind the conversation to an earlier point.

**Profiles** keep several providers side by side, switchable without losing the conversation.

**Tweak and reverse engineering tools** — class and method lookup from the device's own dyld cache, a live class dump from a running app, FairPlay decryption on the phone, and an environment probe that runs each tool instead of looking for it.

Step-by-step instructions are in the **Usage** tab.

## Providers

**OpenRouter** signs in through the browser — no key to copy — and reaches Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok with one account.

Also built in: DeepSeek · OpenAI · Moonshot (Kimi) · xAI (Grok) · Qwen · Z.ai (GLM) · Groq · Mistral · Together AI · a local Ollama or llama.cpp · any custom OpenAI-compatible endpoint.

## Node.js is bundled

Install shiv and it runs. Nothing else to add.

## Requirements

- iOS 15 or newer
- **rootless** (Dopamine / Procursus) → the `iphoneos-arm64` package
- **RootHide** → the `iphoneos-arm64e` package
- Your own API key, or an OpenRouter account for browser sign-in

Built and used on iPhone 15 Pro (iOS 17.0.3, RootHide) and iPhone XS (iOS 16.1.1, Dopamine rootless). Rootful jailbreaks are untested.

**Limits.** `.appex` extensions run in their own process and aren't decrypted by this route. Class lookup is verified on iOS 16 and 17; on another version shiv says it can't confirm a name rather than returning a wrong one.

```
shiv
```

First launch asks for language, provider, API key and model.

Run it as **mobile**, not as root. Under root the files it writes end up owned by root and `~/.shiv` stops being writable.

**OpenRouter — no key to copy.** Pick OpenRouter in the wizard and the browser sign-in starts by itself: Safari opens the approval page, you confirm with your OpenRouter account, and the key comes back to the app. If the browser cannot be opened automatically, type the short address it prints (`http://127.0.0.1:<port>`) into any browser on the device.

**Any other provider** — paste your key at the key step.

Settings live in `~/.shiv` and survive upgrades. Sessions are stored locally in `~/.shiv/oturumlar`.

Shell commands and file writes always ask first. What counts as "ask every time" is set in `/permissions`, and `/preferences` covers the rest of the behaviour.

Reading files, listing directories and searching don't ask.

Requirements and supported jailbreaks are on the **Details** tab.
Command names follow the interface language (`/lang`), so `/login` and `/giriş` are the same command. A prefix is enough — `/prof`.

views.markdown: A job sent to the background keeps running while you type. Press `↓` to reach the counter at the bottom, `Enter` for detail, `k` to stop it, `←` to go back to the list, `Esc` to close. Output appears while the job is still running.

shiv measures the device instead of guessing. Start here:

```
/env
```

Reports theos, the SDK, frida, `oldabi`, the inject directory and the bundled tools — each one actually run, not just looked for, so a broken tool shows as broken.

`/device` scans the device itself: iOS, model, jailbreak, disk. `/mac` and `/remote` set up and check building on a Mac over the network.

### On PATH after install

```
shiv-sinif <name>          class/method search from the dyld cache (no frida)
shiv-oku <bundle-id>       live ObjC class dump from a running app (frida)
shiv-cek <bundle-id>       FairPlay decrypt, on the device itself (frida)
shiv-frida-kur             diagnose frida: binary, package, agent, daemon,
                           conflicts and leftovers
```

`TWEAK.md` ships with the package and holds the recipes the assistant follows.

`shiv-oku` and `shiv-cek` need **frida-server 16.x** — the client is linked against frida-core 16, so a 17.x server cannot talk to it.

```
shiv-frida-kur
```

Reports what you have and changes nothing: binary, package, agent, daemon, conflicts and leftovers. It installs the matching 16.1.4 only when you ask:

```
sudo shiv-frida-kur --kur
```

Rootless takes the GitHub release deb; RootHide takes it from the RootHide repo, which is unsigned and needs `--allow-unauthenticated`. The version is then held so an update can't replace it with 17.x.

Tweaks for App Store apps and command line tools build on the phone with nothing to think about.

System process tweaks are arm64e, and the on-device compiler emits an older pointer authentication ABI. Two things in your code trip it: an `@"..."` string literal, and handing a **block** to the system. Hooks, selector calls and ivar reads are fine.

`oldabi` bridges both, and `/env` reports whether you have it. It does not cover **Swift** — the Swift runtime authenticates its own pointers somewhere `oldabi` never reaches, so a Swift arm64e tweak built on the phone still crashes. That one has to be built on a Mac. For a package other people will install, declare it:

```
Depends: firmware (<< 15.0) | cy+cpu.arm64v8 | oldabi
```

Or connect a Mac with `/mac` and build there for a deb that depends on nothing. Both routes work; shiv explains the difference instead of pushing one.

```
SHIV_OLUK='╰' shiv
```

Changes the gutter glyph. Use it if your terminal draws the default one at the wrong width — lines will look one column short.

```
SHIV_ANLATIM_KATLA=1
```

Folds the assistant's narration as well as tool output.

```
SHIV_NODE_CAPRAZ=1
```

Builds debs on a Mac without a device attached.

### Signing in

**OpenRouter signs in through the browser.** No key to copy any more. Pick OpenRouter in the wizard and the login page opens on its own; approve it in Safari and the key comes back. If the page doesn't open, a short `127.0.0.1` address can be typed by hand. A failure names its stage: port, timeout, refusal, exchange or cancel.

**`/login`** signs in from scratch. **`/key`** shows the key masked, with `yenile` to replace it, `sil` to sign out and `aç` to reveal it.

**Provider list reordered.** OpenRouter first — one browser login, one key for Claude, GPT, Gemini and Grok — then DeepSeek, OpenAI, Moonshot (Kimi), xAI, and two new ones, **Qwen** and **Z.ai**. Default models updated.

**Model lists page properly.** A 455-model list used to wrap back to the start after nine entries. `←` and `→` move by page, and the same paging now applies to every panel.

### Profiles

- `/profil` carries its own actions — **add a profile** and **delete a profile** sit in the list itself
- Deleting asks twice; the address, model and key go together
- Half-written subcommands match by prefix instead of being read as a profile name

### frida

**`shiv-frida-kur` checks first and installs nothing.** The default run changes nothing on the device: binary, package, agent, plist, process, plus the states that quietly break an install — two separate binaries, an orphan binary, a package with no binary, a server with no agent, a process left in memory, a version mismatch, a leftover deb. Installing is now an explicit `sudo shiv-frida-kur --kur`.

**Both layouts are handled** — rootless from the GitHub release deb, RootHide from the RootHide repo, which is unsigned and needs `--allow-unauthenticated`.

**A frida that wasn't running no longer reports as running.** The check matched any process carrying the string on its command line. It asks for the process name now.

**No more false conflict warning** on RootHide, where two paths can be the same file.

### Interface

- Wrapped dim lines no longer turn white halfway through
- Full-width `＋` replaced with ASCII, which the terminal counts correctly

### Packaging

- The source archive is produced again; its root was pinned to one path and failed silently on every build
- Mac cross-build produces both architectures with no device attached
- 51 tests have to pass before a package is produced

**`shiv-sinif` works again.** `dsc-disk.js` was never copied into the package, so a clean install always died with `ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND`. Added, and the packaging now verifies it.

**`/env` runs the tools instead of looking for the files.** It used to report `ok` for tools that were broken. A tool that fails now shows as failed.

**`shivfrida` disappeared on every reinstall.** `postrm` had no guard, so a dpkg upgrade deleted the directory that had just been unpacked. Cleanup is bound to `remove|purge` now, as Debian expects.

**frida version.** shiv links frida-core 16, so the server has to be 16.x — the repo's latest is 17.x and will not talk to it. On rootless, `shiv-frida-kur` fetches a matching 16.1.4 and pins it.

**`shiv-cek` on rootless** returned empty fields because the Dopamine bootstrap has no `awk`; rewritten with `tr` and `cut`. It also finds `shivfrida` from its own location instead of a hard-coded path.

**Mac cross-build** — with `SHIV_NODE_CAPRAZ=1` the bundled iOS node is verified as a Mach-O rather than executed, so debs can be produced on a Mac without a device.

### Rootless support, rebuilt

**Environment detection was wrong.** The check was "is `/var/jb` a symlink" — but it is a symlink on Dopamine too, just pointing somewhere else. A rootless device reported itself as RootHide, and every piece of guidance that followed was built on that. It is read from `/rootfs`, `.jbroot-*` and `readlink /var/jb` now.

**`awk` doesn't exist** in the Dopamine bootstrap, so `/env` was saying "no frida" while frida was running. Rewritten with `sed` and `grep`.

**The home directory was a shadow.** `$HOME` points at `/var/jb/var/mobile` on rootless, so `/export` wrote somewhere Files and Filza never show. It uses the real `/var/mobile` now.

**Frida isn't in the default rootless repos.** `/env` says to add `https://build.frida.re/`.

### Guidance follows the environment

Theos flavour, patcher and the recommended build flow are chosen from the device in front of you. A rootless device is no longer told to use the RootHide fork.

`/env` reports **`oldabi`** as well, and the model's guidance was corrected with it: a system-process tweak with a block builds on the phone when `oldabi` is present, and needs it declared in `Depends` for anyone else. A Mac build is the alternative, not the only route.

### Packaging

`shiv-cek`, `shiv-oku` and `shivfrida` were documented but never shipped — `paketle.sh` only copied `shiv-sinif` and `shiv-ortam`. All three are in the deb now (shivfrida 14 MB, arm64e), and packaging ends by extracting them back out of the deb to verify. A missing one stops the build.

### Interface

- Assistant narration is no longer folded; only tool output is (`SHIV_ANLATIM_KATLA=1` restores the old behaviour)
- `Ctrl+G` send-now works again; queued messages show under the spinner
- The language step previews its description in the language under the cursor
- `/env` output reads more cleanly — separate blocks, neutral tone

shiv can now build tweaks end to end, on the device.

### Tweak development

**Class and method lookup** — reads the device's own shared cache, and now also binaries that live outside it (Control Centre modules, Settings bundles, SDKs embedded in apps).

**On-device decryption** — `shiv-cek <bundle-id>` unwraps FairPlay without a Mac or Python. `shiv-oku` lists classes from a running app.

**`/env`** — measures the development environment before work starts: jailbreak type, Theos path and flavour, SDKs, frida, and the build flow it recommends.

**Build guidance** — the model knows which tweaks can be built on the phone and which need a Mac, and explains the difference instead of refusing flatly.

**`TWEAK.md`** ships with the package: recipes the model reads when it needs them, so the base prompt stays small.

### Background tasks

`Ctrl+B` sends a running job to the background. `↓` reaches the counter, `Enter` opens detail, `k` stops it. Output streams while the job is still running, and the timer ticks every second.

### Fixed

- **Lines were losing their last character.** The gutter mark `⎿` draws two columns in this terminal while shiv counted one, so every gutter line shifted a column and later redraws clipped the end. Now `└`.
- Command tails (`exit=1`, elapsed time) overflowed the width budget
- `Ctrl+B` was bound twice; the background branch was unreachable
- Fold state is saved, so `/resume` no longer reopens collapsed text
- Sessions broken by a half-finished tool call are repaired on load
- Mac connection and respring now go through the permission prompt

### Documentation

A standalone tweak development guide ships in `belgeler/` — readable on its own, without shiv.

### New

**Class and method lookup** — shiv reads your device's own system libraries, so tweak code uses real names instead of guesses.

**Remote build** — connect a Mac with `/mac` and build there without leaving the app.

**`/device`** — disk, conflicting tweaks, crash history, broken packages.

**`/export`** — export a session to a file, API keys stripped.

**`BILGI.md`** — your own notes, given to the model every session.

**Context trimming** — long conversations no longer hit the wall.

### Changed

- Smaller install: 96 → 71 MB
- The model now refuses on-device builds that would trigger Safe Mode, and explains what to do instead

### Fixed

- Setup screen accepted the API key but would not advance
- Working directory could silently reset to the install path
- Crash logs and system paths under `/rootfs` were unreachable
- Long tool sessions could stop without saying why
**Fixed** — entering the API key on the setup screen.

**Node.js is bundled now.** Nothing else to install, on RootHide or rootless.

### New

**Sub-agents — the model can delegate.** Large jobs get split into background sub-tasks that run in parallel: one searches files while another reads logs, and the results come back merged.

**Performance presets** — `/performance`. High, Balanced or Low power. Controls whether markdown is styled while streaming, how often the screen redraws, and how much history stays live.

**Rewind** — take the conversation back to an earlier point. Press `Esc` twice, pick a point, continue from there.

**Background tasks** — `Ctrl+B` sends a running job to the background and tells you when it finishes.

**Startup hints** — short tips appear on the right when you open the app, then fade on their own.

### Changed

**Speed.** Typing, streaming and scrolling were rebuilt. Long sessions no longer slow down; the keyboard stays instant even after hundreds of messages.

**Response time.** The app was sending more than it needed to on every message. Replies start sooner now.

**Look.** New logo, consistent across the app, the icon and this page.

### Fixed

- Wrapped lines keep their indentation
- Code blocks stay inside their border when wrapped
- Arrow keys and `Esc` no longer drop keystrokes
- Held backspace no longer jumps the cursor
- Arrow keys no longer get stuck on commands in history
- A crash on launch
- Streaming slowing down on long replies

**New** — `/context` and `/about`, plus a detailed activity view on `Ctrl+O`.

**Changed** — `/model`, `/profile` and `/lang` are pickable lists now instead of typed arguments. `/settings` reorganised. Panels behave consistently with each other. Clearer message when you interrupt a reply.

**Fixed** — duplicate welcome card; model selection getting lost; Turkish strings showing up in the English interface; words breaking mid-word at the edge; session picker breaking on rotation; command names getting truncated.

**Better** — fewer screen refreshes, and opening or closing the keyboard no longer resizes the panels.

**Rotation is smooth now.** Turning the device reflows the screen to the new width and keeps your conversation with it.

**No more flicker.** Only the parts that actually changed get redrawn, while typing and while a reply streams in.

**Landscape welcome card** — logo on the left, shortcuts and working directory on the right.

**Three new themes.** Switch with `/theme`.

**Command list is navigable.** Walk it with the arrow keys, filter it as you type.

**Working directories** added with `/add-dir` are clearer in the panel.

**Help panel reworked** — two columns in landscape, full description of the selected command in portrait.

- Verified on a rootless device — the rootless build is no longer untested
- Node.js is now in this repo for both RootHide and rootless, so it installs alongside shiv
- Language handling fixed
- `/geo` output reworked

First release.

- Sessions are saved every turn and can be continued or searched
- Several providers side by side, switchable without losing context
- Turkish and English throughout, including the reply language
- Input history with arrow keys and `Ctrl+R` search
- Output panel on `Ctrl+T`
- Multi-line paste arrives as one message instead of one per line
- Two builds: rootless and RootHide
